<p class="print-note">Eight settings. Cut along the dashed lines and deal one
per team. Cards 1–4 suit meeting 7 (experiments, instruments,
discontinuities); cards 5–8 suit meeting 8 (difference-in-differences, fixed
effects, event studies). Page&nbsp;2 is the defence sheet.</p>

<div class="sheetwrap">
<div class="cards">

  <div class="card">
    <span class="n">Card 1 · <span>meeting 7</span></span>
    <h3>The savings nudge</h3>
    <p>A bank wants to know whether its monthly financial-literacy email
    makes customers save more. It has 400,000 customers on the list, it
    controls who receives what, and it can wait six months.</p>
    <p class="ask"><b>Defend:</b> what design, and what does it cost them to run it properly?</p>
  </div>

  <div class="card">
    <span class="n">Card 2 · <span>meeting 7</span></span>
    <h3>The scholarship cutoff</h3>
    <p>A university awards a scholarship to every applicant scoring above
    1200 on an entrance test, and to nobody below. Administrators want to
    know whether the money raises graduation rates.</p>
    <p class="ask"><b>Defend:</b> what design — and who exactly does your estimate apply to?</p>
  </div>

  <div class="card">
    <span class="n">Card 3 · <span>meeting 7</span></span>
    <h3>The water filters</h3>
    <p>An NGO distributed water filters to the villages that asked for
    them. Diarrhoea rates fell in those villages and not in others. The
    donor wants to know whether the filters worked.</p>
    <p class="ask"><b>Defend:</b> a design — or defend the claim that this cannot honestly be answered.</p>
  </div>

  <div class="card">
    <span class="n">Card 4 · <span>meeting 7</span></span>
    <h3>The local label</h3>
    <p>A food company is deciding whether to put "locally sourced" on a
    package. It wants to know what that claim is worth in cents per unit
    before it commits to the supply chain.</p>
    <p class="ask"><b>Defend:</b> what design, and what is the gap between what it measures and what they want?</p>
  </div>

  <div class="card">
    <span class="n">Card 5 · <span>meeting 8</span></span>
    <h3>The self-checkout rollout</h3>
    <p>A grocery chain installed self-checkout in 340 of its 900 stores
    over eighteen months, region by region, in an order set by an old
    refurbishment schedule. Did basket size change?</p>
    <p class="ask"><b>Defend:</b> what design — and what does "region by region" buy you?</p>
  </div>

  <div class="card">
    <span class="n">Card 6 · <span>meeting 8</span></span>
    <h3>The border wage</h3>
    <p>One state raised its minimum wage on 1 January; the state across
    the river did not. There are fast-food restaurants within two miles
    of the border on both sides.</p>
    <p class="ask"><b>Defend:</b> what design, and what has to be true about the two sides?</p>
  </div>

  <div class="card">
    <span class="n">Card 7 · <span>meeting 8</span></span>
    <h3>The light rail</h3>
    <p>A city opened a light-rail line four years ago. House prices within
    half a mile of the new stations are up 22% since. The transit
    authority would like to claim credit.</p>
    <p class="ask"><b>Defend:</b> what design — and why is the naive comparison almost certainly wrong?</p>
  </div>

  <div class="card">
    <span class="n">Card 8 · <span>meeting 8</span></span>
    <h3>The seller fee</h3>
    <p>A platform raised its commission for seller accounts created on or
    after 1 March, leaving older accounts on the old rate. It wants to
    know whether the higher fee drove sellers away.</p>
    <p class="ask"><b>Defend:</b> what design, and what would make the two groups not comparable?</p>
  </div>

</div>
